title: fix(plugin-auth): disabling an OAuth client refuses its already-issued tokens on the next call, and an administrator's API-key suspension holds against the owner
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-zhuang"} -->
_Requested by **Sam** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HP?thread=cmsg_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HPErHnZPyo1CbWaKqz1dkrEt)_

Closes objectstack-ai/objectstack#31606

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：停用 OAuth 客户端后，它已经发出去的访问令牌在下一次调用就被 MCP 入口拒绝（401）；平台管理员吊销别人的 API 密钥时记下「已被管理员暂停」，密钥所有者不能自己恢复，只有平台管理员能恢复。
- 为什么改：实测停用客户端后旧令牌照样能用，直到 1 小时后过期；管理员吊销的密钥，所有者马上就能点「恢复」。管理员的「立刻停掉」两头都不生效。
- 风险与回滚：每次 MCP 调用多一次按 client_id 的索引读取；读取失败按拒绝处理。回滚就是还原这个 PR，不涉及数据迁移。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-token-revocation.ts`（`mcpConsentAdmits`），`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/api-key-restore-guard.ts`（`stampSuspension`）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/mcp-token-revocation.test.ts src/api-key-restore-guard.test.ts`，预期全部通过，其中新增的 card 2 用例共 12 个。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

**OAuth clients: a disabled client's live tokens.** The MCP door's per-call grant read (`mcpConsentAdmits`, `mcp-token-revocation.ts`) now reads the client row first, through the same better-auth adapter it reads the consent through. A token is refused (the verifier answers `null`, so the door answers the existing `401`) when the client is disabled, when its row is gone, or when the read fails. A server-only `skip_consent` client's flag is read off that same row, so the consent-less path costs no extra read. The provider already refused a disabled client new tokens (`invalid_client` at the token endpoint, `client_disabled` at authorize, inactive at introspection) by the same truthy test on the same column; only this door read none of it. Disabling is a pause, not an end: the consent and the refresh family stay, so enabling the client again serves the same grant. Ending a grant stays the withdraw or `/oauth2/revoke`. Cost: two indexed reads per MCP call (client by unique `client_id`, then consent) instead of one.

**API keys: an administrator's stop holds against the owner.** This corrects the card's premise (agreed in the cloud#3820 PM thread): `sys_api_key.revoked` is **not** terminal. The Revoke API Key / Restore API Key row actions already make it reversible, and only `organization_membership_ended` makes it final. The real gap was that an owner could restore a key a platform administrator had revoked the moment it was revoked. So, per the ruling in that thread (option A, no new column, no new state):

- `revoked_reason` gains a third value, `administrator_suspended` (`sys-api-key.object.ts`, label and description translated in all nine shipped locales).
- The restore guard (`api-key-restore-guard.ts`, rule 4) stamps it on a user-context revoke by a caller with platform-admin standing who is not the row's `user_id`, when the row carries no reason yet. A host that stops a key itself (cloud's console, in the system context) writes the same value beside `revoked: true`; system writes are never stamped or refused.
- Rule 2 extends to it: only a platform administrator restores such a key. The owner's restore is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, naming the reason and both roads. Restore clears the reason, as before, and the same key works with no re-issue.
- An administrator's revoke never replaces a reason the key already carries, so `organization_membership_ended` stays final.
- A multi-row update shares one payload, so a stamp written for one row lands on every row. A multi-row admin revoke that matches both a row the rule stamps and a row that already carries a different reason is refused whole with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, in either row order, before the driver writes. A batch of plain keys is stamped on every row. Over-stamping an administrator's own key in such a batch is harmless, because the administrator can restore it.
- The key door's `403 API_KEY_REVOKED` text (`@objectstack/core` `api-key.ts`) gets an arm that names a platform administrator as the only restorer.

⚠️ **Still open, by design, and owned elsewhere:** this closes the owner's *restore*, not the owner's *new key*. A person who may mint keys can still mint a fresh one, and it acts as them. An AI service account whose credentials only administrators issue closes that gap (cloud#3820 O1/O3, objectstack#31603). This PR does not try to solve it.

## Step-1 measurement (before the fix)

Real routes, in-process HTTP, on objectstack `158cc2aa` (main when measured): the showcase dogfood stack with `MCPServerPlugin`, `OS_OIDC_PROVIDER_ENABLED=true`. Flow: DCR public client, sign-in, authorize (PKCE, `resource` = the MCP URL), consent, code exchange.

<details><summary>OAuth client disable: the old token kept working</summary>

| Step | Answer |
|:--|:--|
| access-token lifetime | `expires_in` 3600, `exp − iat` = 3600 s |
| `POST /mcp` initialize, before the disable | 200 |
| `POST /auth/admin/oauth2/toggle-disabled {disabled: true}` as the platform admin | 200 |
| `POST /mcp` initialize, **same token** | **200, served** (the defect) |
| `refresh_token` grant while disabled | 400 `invalid_client` "client is disabled" |
| enable again: the same token / its refresh | 200 / 200 |

</details>

<details><summary>API key: the owner undid an administrator's revoke</summary>

| Step | Answer |
|:--|:--|
| member mints a key (`POST /api/v1/keys`), key works | 201, then 200 |
| platform admin `PATCH /data/sys_api_key/{id} {revoked: true}` | 200; the key then answers 403 `API_KEY_REVOKED` |
| **member** `PATCH /data/sys_api_key/{id} {revoked: false}` | **200**; the key works again (the hole) |

</details>

## Tests

_Two commits after this section was written seed a client row in three existing verifier test files (26 cases that read no client row) and update three docs pages; the os-dev-report on #31606 covers both._

New pins, each as a top-level `describe` in that component's existing harness file:

- `plugin-auth` `mcp-token-revocation.test.ts`, on the real `AuthManager` and the installed provider (4 cases): a token minted before the disable is refused, its refresh is refused by the provider, the grant rows stay, and once enabled again the same token and a refreshed one verify; a disabled `skip_consent` client is refused; a token whose client row is gone is refused; a store error in the client read refuses. **All 4 red on the old verifier** (restored from `origin/main` while the tests stayed): `expected { …(3) } to be null`.
- `plugin-auth` `api-key-restore-guard.test.ts`, on the real engine, `SecurityPlugin`, D2 guard and key door (8 cases): the stamp, the owner's 403, the admin's restore and the key working again; CONTROL: an admin's own key gets no reason; an owner-revoked key re-revoked by an admin is stamped; an owner's re-revoke and smuggled clear keep it; an admin's revoke keeps `organization_membership_ended` and `admin_password_reset`; a host's system suspension holds; a plain multi-row revoke stamps every row; a mixed multi-row revoke is refused whole in both orders. **6 of 8 red on the old guard.** The 2 that stay green are the controls that hold today too.
- `plugin-auth` `forced-reset-revoke-reason-vocabulary.test.ts`: the option list is exactly the three values, and the description names the new one.
- `core` `api-key-lifecycle.test.ts`: the door text for `administrator_suspended` names only a platform administrator.
- `dogfood` `authorized-client-withdraw.dogfood.test.ts`, over HTTP: a member's toggle is refused 403 and moves nothing; the admin's disable makes the same bearer **401 at `/mcp`** and its refresh `400 invalid_client`, while the consent stays; enabled again, the same token, a refreshed token and a new person's consent on the same client are all served. **Red against the old `plugin-auth` build** (`expected 200 to be 401`), green after rebuilding.
- `dogfood` `api-key-owner-revoke.dogfood.test.ts`, over HTTP: the admin's `revoke_api_key` PATCH refuses the member's key on its next call and stores `administrator_suspended`; the member's `restore_api_key` PATCH is 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`; the admin's restore brings the same key back and clears the reason; CONTROL: the member's own revoke and restore work as before.

Both dogfood files had their boot and helpers hoisted from inside the existing `describe` to module scope, so the new `describe` shares the one showcase boot. `git diff -w` shows that move as a few lines.

## Acceptance notes

- **Declaration lines** (seat 3 confirmed the changeset's reading on review: `patch` for all three packages, precedent objectstack#31435) are at the top of this body.
- **Re-enable revives the outstanding grant**, the access token and its refresh alike. That is deliberate, because the card's "one-click disable" is recoverable. A client that must lose its grants for good is withdrawn or revoked.
- **No new error code.** The OAuth refusal is the existing 401. The key refusal stays `API_KEY_REVOKED`, and the restore refusal `PERMISSION_DENIED`. The mixed-batch refusal is `VALIDATION_ERROR`, reachable only from an in-process multi-row user-context write, because `sys_api_key` has no batch route.
- **Who stamps.** Only a caller with platform-admin standing (`hasPlatformAdminStanding`) who is not the row's owner. The shipped permission sets let no one else write another person's key (`sys_api_key_self`), so in a shipped composition that is every non-owner revoke.

## Verification

See the os-dev-report on the card for package suites, typecheck and the dispatch-gate sweep at the final head.
